_comment_set_cookie_attribute_cases: RFC 6265 sec. 4.1.1: only the first segment of a Set-Cookie value is cookie data; the reserved attributes after it scope the cookie and must survive. Expected values assume no hasher (plain [REDACTED] placeholder).

url_token_login_cases._comment: URL-token login: the client appends <prefix>_<base64(user:pass)> as a bare query segment. queryString is what Playwright records: URLSearchParams splits at the first '=' and decodes '+' to a space and %3D to '='. The credential forms must not survive anywhere in the sanitized HAR, the prefix must, and validate must find nothing left to report.

url_valued_header_cases._comment: A request URL's query is repeated in the next request's Referer, and a redirect's Location can carry one. Each header value must come out without the leaked forms, and validate must report the raw file and pass the sanitized one.

transport_encoded_body_cases._comment: Response bodies through _sanitize_response_content. A transport-encoded (encoding: base64) body is decoded first and handled as the text it carries, then written back as plain text with 'encoding' dropped; binary stays base64 and untouched. expect_encoding is the 'encoding' left on the content (null: none). absent must not survive, present must; text_equals pins the whole output, text_suffix its end. Bodies without encoding exercise the sniff for mime types that do not route themselves.

cases._note: Transport-encoded HTML fragment whose text has a colon: was wiped to AUTH_
Survived before, but no sanitizer pass reached it
The body is base64(user:pass) inside transport base64
_patch_missing_bodies base64-encodes a text body that is not UTF-8
An earlier release wiped the body to AUTH_ and kept encoding: base64, which no decoder accepts
Broadcast and zero MACs are protocol constants scripts compare against
Capture stores a page base64 when its bytes are not UTF-8, whatever it declares

base64_query_payload_cases._comment: A query value (or bare segment) that is base64 of a JSON object/array or a URL is a payload, not a credential, whatever its padding: it is decoded, sanitized inside, and re-encoded — unpadded only where the original visibly stripped padding, percent-encoded where it was — or left byte-identical when nothing inside needed redacting. A payload wins over an identity-style name, as in validate. leaked must not survive in the URL, the queryString array, or the decoded payload; decoded_present must appear in the decoded payload.

deep_nesting_cases._comment: JSON nested past the parser's recursion limit, on every surface that parses JSON: sanitize and validate must both finish. The test builds each surface from its id.

json_identity_body_cases._comment: JSON bodies through the sanitizer: a key that names a serial or MAC (classify_identity_field) and holds a value of that shape is redacted — SERIAL_<hash>, or a MAC placeholder in the value's own layout — and nothing else under such a key is. A body is JSON when its text parses as a JSON object or array, whatever type it declares (HNAP answers as text/html). absent must not survive; present must. pad prefixes that many characters of filler, for a body past the old 1 MB scan limit.

value_pass_body_cases._comment: JSON values, JSON keys and plain-text bodies get the same format-preserving value passes as the HTML engine (MAC, private and public IPv4, IPv6, email), from the same shared regexes, and its labeled-serial passes on the raw text; nest_lists wraps the body in that many arrays, past the key rules' depth; the IPv6 constants :: and ::1 stay in both. Keys are sanitized as text because a client table keyed by MAC or address is a PII shape validate reports. absent must not survive; present must.

custom_preserved_gateway_cases._comment: A caller's preserved_gateway_ips (custom_patterns) are kept on every route, not only the HTML engine's: the string patterns resolve them from the same per-call scope.

no_collector_body_cases._comment: _sanitize_response_content called without a collector (the library's lowest-level entry): nothing to hash with, so the positional passes are skipped and the string patterns write their static placeholders.

post_text_cases._comment: sanitize_post_data on postData.text: urlencoded and XML by type, JSON by content whatever the type, any other text through the string patterns. absent must not survive; present must.

cross_route_correlation_cases._comment: One value in bodies of every route gets one placeholder: the engines share regexes, validity rules, pass order and hasher, so a consumer can follow it across the capture. template holds {v}; placeholder is the regex its replacement must match, in every body; a case's own bodies replace the shared ones (a value two passes could claim: a MAC after a serial label, an address in a credential's element).
